answer: Each identity stakes a shale layer onto a public stack: registering the Nth identity requires re-attesting every layer beneath it, so N identities cost O(N²) work, not N. All layers sit in one open ocean ledger, so a clone reusing a sediment fingerprint is visible to everyone at once. At each dawn the oldest layer faces a pressure audit; if it fails, the whole column above it is slashed together, so stacking clones multiplies the loss instead of spreading it.
